name: LOLCODE
title: LOLCODE 1.2
intro: LOLCODE was made in 2007 as a joke about lolcat captions, but it is a complete language with variables, loops, functions and a written specification (version 1.2). Under the silly words it works much like a small scripting language, which makes it a fun way to practise ideas you already know, or to meet them for the first time. To run code yourself, build the lci interpreter from its source (github.com/justinmeza/lci), save a program in a file ending in .lol and run lci file.lol. Every example shows exactly what it prints.

lessons.title: HAI and VISIBLE
lessons.summary: Program bounds, printing, comments and special characters.

sections.p: Every program starts with HAI 1.2 (the version) and ends with KTHXBYE. VISIBLE prints and then starts a new line. BTW starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
BTW this is a comment
VISIBLE "OH HAI"
VISIBLE "I CAN HAS CHEEZBURGER?"
KTHXBYE
sections.out:
OH HAI
I CAN HAS CHEEZBURGER?

sections.p: Give VISIBLE several values and it prints them one after another with nothing in between, so put any spaces inside the quotes. A ! at the very end stops the new line, so the next VISIBLE carries on the same line.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "NUTZ = " 3
VISIBLE "SQUIR"!
VISIBLE "REL"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: OBTW starts a comment that can cover many lines, and TLDR (“too long, didn't read”) ends it.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
OBTW
  This whole part is ignored.
  Even this line.
TLDR
VISIBLE "STILL HERE"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Inside a string the colon is the escape character. :) is a new line, :> a tab, :" a double quote and :: a colon.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "ONE:)TWO"
VISIBLE "SHE SED :"HAI:""
VISIBLE "TIME:: 3 OCLOCK"
KTHXBYE
sections.out:
ONE
TWO
SHE SED "HAI"
TIME: 3 OCLOCK

sections.p: A comma works like a line break, so short statements can share a line.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "A", VISIBLE "B"
KTHXBYE

practice.why: VISIBLE is LOLCODE's print.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "UP" "TREE"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: VISIBLE joins its values with nothing in between.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "HAI"!
VISIBLE "2U"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The ! at the end stops the new line, so 2U follows straight on.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
BTW VISIBLE "SECRET"
VISIBLE "PUBLIC"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The first line is a comment, so it never runs.

practice.q: How do you put a new line inside a string?
practice.why: The colon is LOLCODE's escape character, and :) means a new line.

practice.q: Which word ends a multi-line comment?
practice.why: OBTW opens the comment and TLDR closes it.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "ONE:)TWO"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: :) inside a string is a new line.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE "A", VISIBLE "B", VISIBLE "C"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: A comma acts like a line break, so each VISIBLE runs on its own.

practice.q: What does a ! at the end of VISIBLE do?
options: Stops the new line so the next print continues on the same line
practice.answer: Stops the new line so the next print continues on the same line
practice.why: Without !, VISIBLE always finishes with a new line.

lessons.title: Variables and types
lessons.summary: I HAS A, R, the five types and changing between them.

sections.p: I HAS A name ITZ value makes a variable; name R value changes it. A variable made without ITZ holds NOOB, which means “nothing yet”.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A nuts ITZ 3
VISIBLE "I HAS " nuts " NUTZ"
nuts R 10
VISIBLE "NAO I HAS " nuts " NUTZ"
KTHXBYE
sections.out:
I HAS 3 NUTZ
NAO I HAS 10 NUTZ

sections.p: NUMBR is a whole number, NUMBAR a number with a decimal point, YARN text, TROOF is WIN or FAIL, and NOOB is nothing. A variable can hold any type and switch to another later. A NUMBAR is always shown with two decimal places.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 42
I HAS A f ITZ 2.5
I HAS A s ITZ "ACORN"
I HAS A t ITZ WIN
VISIBLE n " " f " " s " " t
KTHXBYE

sections.p: :{name} inside a string is replaced by the variable's value. It saves splitting the string into pieces.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A who ITZ "CEILING CAT"
VISIBLE "HAI, :{who}!"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: MAEK value A type gives a copy of the value as another type. name IS NOW A type changes the variable itself. A YARN of digits becomes a number this way, and a NUMBAR made into a NUMBR loses everything after the point.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A typed ITZ "12"
I HAS A num ITZ MAEK typed A NUMBR
VISIBLE SUM OF num AN 1
I HAS A f ITZ 7.9
f IS NOW A NUMBR
VISIBLE f
KTHXBYE

sections.p: SMOOSH a AN b AN c MKAY joins its values into one YARN. MKAY marks where the list ends.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A name ITZ SMOOSH "SQUIR" AN "REL" MKAY
VISIBLE name
VISIBLE SMOOSH name AN " NO. " AN 1 MKAY
KTHXBYE

practice.q: How do you set an existing variable x to 5?
options: I HAS A x ITZ 5 again
practice.why: R assigns to a variable that already exists; I HAS A declares a new one.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A x ITZ 1
x R 7
VISIBLE x
KTHXBYE
practice.why: R replaces the value, so x holds 7 when it is printed.

practice.q: What does a variable hold after I HAS A thing?
practice.why: Without ITZ there is no value yet, which LOLCODE calls NOOB.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE 3.5
KTHXBYE
practice.why: A NUMBAR is shown with two decimal places.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A pet ITZ "KITTEH"
VISIBLE "MAH :{pet}"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: :{pet} is swapped for the value of pet.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE SMOOSH "A" AN 1 AN "B" MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: SMOOSH turns each value into text and joins them with nothing between.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 5
n IS NOW A YARN
VISIBLE SMOOSH n AN "!" MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: IS NOW A YARN changes n itself; SMOOSH then joins it with "!".

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A typed ITZ "9"
VISIBLE MAEK typed A NUMBR
KTHXBYE
practice.why: MAEK gives a NUMBR copy of the digit string; VISIBLE shows 9.

options: The end of a SMOOSH (or ALL OF / ANY OF) list
practice.answer: The end of a SMOOSH (or ALL OF / ANY OF) list
practice.why: Variable-length operator lists need MKAY so LOLCODE knows where they stop.

lessons.title: Maths
lessons.summary: Operators that come first, whole and decimal numbers, nesting.

sections.p: Operators come before their two values, joined by AN: SUM OF, DIFF OF, PRODUKT OF, QUOSHUNT OF, MOD OF (remainder), BIGGR OF and SMALLR OF.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE SUM OF 7 AN 3
VISIBLE DIFF OF 7 AN 3
VISIBLE PRODUKT OF 7 AN 3
VISIBLE QUOSHUNT OF 7 AN 3
VISIBLE MOD OF 7 AN 3
VISIBLE BIGGR OF 7 AN 3
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Two NUMBRs give a NUMBR, so QUOSHUNT OF 7 AN 2 is 3: the remainder is dropped. If either side is a NUMBAR, the answer is a NUMBAR.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE QUOSHUNT OF 7 AN 2
VISIBLE QUOSHUNT OF 7.0 AN 2
VISIBLE SUM OF 1 AN 0.25
KTHXBYE

sections.p: An operator can be the value of another. Read from the left: the outer operator waits for both of its values to be worked out. There are no brackets and no precedence to learn.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE PRODUKT OF SUM OF 2 AN 3 AN 4
VISIBLE SUM OF 2 AN PRODUKT OF 3 AN 4
KTHXBYE

sections.p: To add to a variable, assign the sum back to it. Text that holds a number is turned into one when maths needs it.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A score ITZ 10
score R SUM OF score AN 5
score R PRODUKT OF score AN 2
VISIBLE score
VISIBLE SUM OF "4" AN 4
KTHXBYE

practice.why: DIFF OF subtracts the second value from the first.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE QUOSHUNT OF 9 AN 2
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Both values are NUMBRs, so the answer is a NUMBR and the remainder is dropped.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE MOD OF 17 AN 5
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 17 is 3 × 5 with 2 left over.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE DIFF OF PRODUKT OF 3 AN 3 AN 1
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The first value of DIFF OF is PRODUKT OF 3 AN 3, which is 9; 9 − 1 = 8.

practice.q: What does BIGGR OF 3 AN 8 give?
practice.why: BIGGR OF returns the larger of the two.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE SUM OF 1.5 AN 1
KTHXBYE
practice.why: One side is a NUMBAR, so the sum is a NUMBAR, shown with two decimal places.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE PRODUKT OF 5 AN SUM OF 1 AN 1
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The second value of PRODUKT OF is SUM OF 1 AN 1, which is 2; 5 × 2 = 10.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE SMALLR OF 9 AN 2
KTHXBYE
practice.why: SMALLR OF returns the lesser of the two.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE QUOSHUNT OF 9.0 AN 2
KTHXBYE
practice.why: One side is a NUMBAR, so the quotient is a NUMBAR shown with two decimal places.

lessons.title: TROOFs and comparisons
lessons.summary: WIN and FAIL, comparing values, and the IT variable.

sections.p: BOTH SAEM a AN b is WIN when the values are equal; DIFFRINT a AN b is WIN when they differ. There is no “greater than”: instead ask whether a value is the same as the bigger of the two.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE BOTH SAEM 4 AN 4
VISIBLE DIFFRINT 4 AN 5
I HAS A x ITZ 9
VISIBLE BOTH SAEM x AN BIGGR OF x AN 5
KTHXBYE

sections.p: BOTH SAEM does not turn text into numbers, so the YARN "3" is not the same as the NUMBR 3. A NUMBR and a NUMBAR with the same value are equal.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE BOTH SAEM 3 AN "3"
VISIBLE BOTH SAEM 3 AN 3.0
KTHXBYE

sections.p: BOTH OF is “and”, EITHER OF is “or”, WON OF is “one but not both”, and NOT flips a value. ALL OF ... MKAY and ANY OF ... MKAY take a whole list.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE BOTH OF WIN AN FAIL
VISIBLE EITHER OF WIN AN FAIL
VISIBLE WON OF WIN AN WIN
VISIBLE NOT FAIL
VISIBLE ALL OF WIN AN WIN AN FAIL MKAY
KTHXBYE

sections.p: When a TROOF is needed, other values are turned into one: 0, 0.0, the empty string "" and NOOB are FAIL; everything else is WIN.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE NOT 0
VISIBLE NOT ""
VISIBLE NOT "FAIL"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: A line that is just a value, with no VISIBLE or R, stores that value in a special variable called IT. The decisions in the next lessons look at IT.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
SUM OF 20 AN 22
VISIBLE IT
KTHXBYE

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE DIFFRINT 2 AN 2
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The values are the same, so DIFFRINT is FAIL.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE BOTH SAEM "7" AN 7
KTHXBYE
practice.why: A YARN and a NUMBR are different types, so they are not the same.

practice.q: How do you ask whether x is at least 10?
options: BOTH SAEM x AN BIGGR OF x AN 10
practice.answer: BOTH SAEM x AN BIGGR OF x AN 10
practice.why: If x is the bigger of x and 10, then x is 10 or more.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE EITHER OF FAIL AN NOT FAIL
KTHXBYE
practice.why: NOT FAIL is WIN, and EITHER OF needs only one WIN.
Only 0, 0.0, the empty string and NOOB are FAIL; any non-empty text is WIN.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
PRODUKT OF 6 AN 7
VISIBLE IT
KTHXBYE
practice.why: A bare value goes into IT, so IT holds 42.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE BOTH OF WIN AN WIN
KTHXBYE
practice.why: BOTH OF is “and”: both sides are WIN.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE WON OF WIN AN FAIL
KTHXBYE
practice.why: WON OF is “one but not both”; exactly one side is WIN.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE NOT "FAIL"
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Any non-empty YARN counts as WIN, so NOT flips it to FAIL.

lessons.title: O RLY? decisions
lessons.summary: YA RLY, NO WAI, MEBBE and OIC.

sections.p: Work out a TROOF on its own line so it lands in IT, then O RLY? branches on it: YA RLY runs when IT is WIN, NO WAI otherwise, and OIC (“oh, I see”) closes the block.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A temp ITZ 4
BOTH SAEM temp AN SMALLR OF temp AN 10
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "CHILLY"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "WARM"
OIC
KTHXBYE

sections.p: The NO WAI part is optional. If IT is FAIL and there is no NO WAI, nothing happens.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A nuts ITZ 0
nuts
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "SNACK TIME"
OIC
VISIBLE "DONE"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: MEBBE expression is “else if”: when the earlier tests fail, its expression is worked out and its part runs if that is WIN. Only the first matching part runs.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 15
BOTH SAEM n AN 0
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "NONE"
  MEBBE BOTH SAEM n AN SMALLR OF n AN 9
    VISIBLE "FEW"
  MEBBE BOTH SAEM n AN SMALLR OF n AN 99
    VISIBLE "LOTS"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "TOO MANY"
OIC
KTHXBYE

sections.p: A whole O RLY? block can sit inside a part of another one. Indenting is optional, but it makes the shape easy to see.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A hungry ITZ WIN
I HAS A nuts ITZ 2
hungry
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    nuts
    O RLY?
      YA RLY
        VISIBLE "NOM NOM"
      NO WAI
        VISIBLE "GO FIND NUTZ"
    OIC
OIC
KTHXBYE

practice.q: What closes an O RLY? block?
practice.why: OIC (“oh, I see”) ends the conditional.

practice.q: Where does the result of BOTH SAEM go when it stands alone on a line?
practice.why: A bare expression is stored in the special variable IT, which O RLY? tests.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A x ITZ 3
BOTH SAEM x AN 4
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "FOUR"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "NOT FOUR"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 3 is not 4, so IT is FAIL and the NO WAI part runs.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 5
BOTH SAEM n AN 1
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "ONE"
  MEBBE BOTH SAEM n AN 5
    VISIBLE "FIVE"
  MEBBE BOTH SAEM n AN BIGGR OF n AN 2
    VISIBLE "BIG"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Only the first part whose test is WIN runs, even though the last test would also be WIN.
MEBBE has its own test and is tried only when the parts above it failed.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A x ITZ 10
BOTH SAEM x AN BIGGR OF x AN 10
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "GE10"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "LT10"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: x equals BIGGR OF x AN 10, so x is at least 10 and YA RLY runs.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
FAIL
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "YES"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "NO"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Putting FAIL alone stores FAIL in IT, so the NO WAI part runs.

lessons.title: WTF? for many cases
lessons.summary: Matching IT against values with OMG, OMGWTF and GTFO.

sections.p: WTF? compares IT with each OMG value in turn. Running starts at the first match and keeps going into the cases below until it meets GTFO. OMGWTF is the case for anything not listed.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A colour ITZ "GREEN"
colour
WTF?
  OMG "RED"
    VISIBLE "STOP"
    GTFO
  OMG "GREEN"
    VISIBLE "GO"
    GTFO
  OMGWTF
    VISIBLE "WAIT"
OIC
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Leave out GTFO and running carries on into the next case. That is handy when several values should share some steps.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
3
WTF?
  OMG 3
    VISIBLE "THREE"
  OMG 2
    VISIBLE "TWO"
  OMG 1
    VISIBLE "ONE"
    GTFO
  OMG 0
    VISIBLE "ZERO"
OIC
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Each OMG must be a plain value written out, such as a number or a string, not a sum or a variable. For ranges, use O RLY? with MEBBE instead.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
"B"
WTF?
  OMG "A"
    VISIBLE "APPLE"
    GTFO
  OMG "B"
    VISIBLE "BANANA"
    GTFO
  OMGWTF
    VISIBLE "HUH"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: IT matches the second case, and GTFO stops before OMGWTF.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
1
WTF?
  OMG 1
    VISIBLE "A"
  OMG 2
    VISIBLE "B"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: There is no GTFO, so running falls through from case 1 into case 2.

practice.q: What does GTFO do inside WTF?
practice.why: GTFO breaks out of the case block, like break in other languages.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
7
WTF?
  OMG 1
    VISIBLE "ONE"
    GTFO
  OMGWTF
    VISIBLE "SOMETHING ELSE"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 7 matches no OMG, so the OMGWTF case runs.

practice.q: Which can be written after OMG?
practice.why: Cases must be plain values, not expressions or variables.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
2
WTF?
  OMG 1
    VISIBLE "ONE"
    GTFO
  OMG 2
    VISIBLE "TWO"
  OMG 3
    VISIBLE "THREE"
    GTFO
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Match starts at OMG 2 with no GTFO, so it falls through into OMG 3.

options: The case that runs when no OMG matched
practice.answer: The case that runs when no OMG matched
practice.why: OMGWTF is the default case, like else in a switch.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.summary: IM IN YR, UPPIN and NERFIN, TIL and WILE, and GTFO.

sections.p: IM IN YR name starts a loop and IM OUTTA YR name ends it. UPPIN YR var adds 1 to a counter after each round, and TIL says when to stop. The counter always starts at 0 and belongs to the loop: it is gone once the loop ends, so give it a name of its own.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR hop UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 3
  VISIBLE "HOP " i
IM OUTTA YR hop
KTHXBYE

sections.p: NERFIN takes 1 away, so the counter goes 0, −1, −2 and so on. WILE is the opposite of TIL: keep going while the test is WIN. The test is checked before every round, so a loop can run zero times.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR count NERFIN YR i WILE DIFFRINT i AN -3
  VISIBLE SUM OF 3 AN i "..."
IM OUTTA YR count
VISIBLE "LIFTOFF"
KTHXBYE

sections.p: A variable made before the loop can collect a total. This adds 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A total ITZ 0
IM IN YR add UPPIN YR k TIL BOTH SAEM k AN 6
  total R SUM OF total AN k
IM OUTTA YR add
VISIBLE total
KTHXBYE

sections.h: GTFO and loops with no test
sections.p: A loop with no UPPIN and no TIL runs until a GTFO inside it. Here the program doubles a number until it passes 100.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A x ITZ 1
IM IN YR grow
  x R PRODUKT OF x AN 2
  BOTH SAEM x AN BIGGR OF x AN 100
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      GTFO
  OIC
IM OUTTA YR grow
VISIBLE x
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Give each loop its own name and counter. The inner loop runs all the way through on every round of the outer one.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR row UPPIN YR r TIL BOTH SAEM r AN 3
  IM IN YR col UPPIN YR c TIL BOTH SAEM c AN 4
    VISIBLE "*"!
  IM OUTTA YR col
  VISIBLE ""
IM OUTTA YR row
KTHXBYE

practice.q: How many times does VISIBLE run in IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 3?
practice.why: i starts at 0 and the loop stops when it reaches 3: rounds 0, 1 and 2.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 4
  VISIBLE i!
IM OUTTA YR l
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The counter starts at 0 and stops before printing 4; the ! keeps it on one line.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR l NERFIN YR n WILE DIFFRINT n AN -2
  VISIBLE n
IM OUTTA YR l
KTHXBYE
practice.why: n starts at 0 and counts down; the loop stops as soon as n is −2, before printing it.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A t ITZ 0
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR k TIL BOTH SAEM k AN 4
  t R SUM OF t AN 2
IM OUTTA YR l
VISIBLE t
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The body runs four times (k = 0 to 3), adding 2 each time.

practice.q: What stops a loop that has no TIL or WILE?
practice.why: GTFO inside a loop breaks out of it.

practice.q: What is the difference between TIL and WILE?
options: TIL stops when the test is WIN; WILE stops when it is FAIL
practice.answer: TIL stops when the test is WIN; WILE stops when it is FAIL
practice.why: TIL means “until” and WILE means “while”.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A t ITZ 1
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 3
  t R PRODUKT OF t AN 2
IM OUTTA YR l
VISIBLE t
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The body runs three times (i = 0, 1, 2), doubling 1 → 2 → 4 → 8.

practice.q: What does UPPIN YR i do each round?
options: Adds 1 to i after the body
practice.answer: Adds 1 to i after the body
practice.why: UPPIN is the loop's increment; NERFIN subtracts 1 instead.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.summary: HOW IZ I, FOUND YR, several parameters and recursion.

sections.p: HOW IZ I name YR param defines a function, FOUND YR value hands back a result, and IF U SAY SO ends it. Call it with I IZ name YR value MKAY.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I dubbl YR n
  FOUND YR PRODUKT OF n AN 2
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ dubbl YR 21 MKAY
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Join extra parameters with AN YR, both when defining and when calling.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I area YR w AN YR h
  FOUND YR PRODUKT OF w AN h
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ area YR 3 AN YR 4 MKAY
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Inside a function you can only see its parameters, the variables it makes, and its own IT. Variables from the main program are out of reach, so pass in anything it needs. A function does not have to hand anything back: this one just prints. GTFO leaves a function early with no value (NOOB).
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I greet YR who
  VISIBLE "HAI " who
IF U SAY SO
I IZ greet YR "BUCKY" MKAY
I IZ greet YR "ROCKY" MKAY
KTHXBYE

sections.p: FOUND YR can sit inside an O RLY?. It leaves the function straight away.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I sign YR n
  BOTH SAEM n AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      FOUND YR "ZERO"
  OIC
  BOTH SAEM n AN BIGGR OF n AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      FOUND YR "PLUS"
  OIC
  FOUND YR "MINUS"
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ sign YR 5 MKAY
VISIBLE I IZ sign YR -2 MKAY
VISIBLE I IZ sign YR 0 MKAY
KTHXBYE

sections.p: A function may call itself, as long as some case stops it. The factorial of n is n × (n − 1) × … × 1.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I fact YR n
  BOTH SAEM n AN SMALLR OF n AN 1
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      FOUND YR 1
  OIC
  FOUND YR PRODUKT OF n AN I IZ fact YR DIFF OF n AN 1 MKAY
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ fact YR 5 MKAY
KTHXBYE

practice.q: How does a LOLCODE function return a value?
practice.why: GTFO leaves without a value; FOUND YR hands one back.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I plus1 YR n
  FOUND YR SUM OF n AN 1
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ plus1 YR I IZ plus1 YR 1 MKAY MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The inner call gives 2, and the outer call adds one more.

practice.q: Which line ends a function definition?
practice.why: HOW IZ I opens the function and IF U SAY SO closes it.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I smaller YR a AN YR b
  FOUND YR SMALLR OF a AN b
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ smaller YR 8 AN YR 3 MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The function hands back the smaller of its two parameters.

practice.q: Can a function read a variable made in the main program?
options: No, pass it in as a parameter
Only if it is a YARN
practice.answer: No, pass it in as a parameter
practice.why: A function has its own scope: its parameters, its own variables and its own IT.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I sum YR n
  BOTH SAEM n AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      FOUND YR 0
  OIC
  FOUND YR SUM OF n AN I IZ sum YR DIFF OF n AN 1 MKAY
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ sum YR 4 MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0, stopping when n reaches 0.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I sq YR n
  FOUND YR PRODUKT OF n AN n
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ sq YR 6 MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: The function returns n × n; 6 × 6 = 36.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
HOW IZ I add3 YR a AN YR b AN YR c
  FOUND YR SUM OF a AN SUM OF b AN c
IF U SAY SO
VISIBLE I IZ add3 YR 1 AN YR 2 AN YR 3 MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Extra parameters use AN YR; 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

practice.q: How do you add a second parameter when defining a function?
practice.why: HOW IZ I f YR a AN YR b … matches the call I IZ f YR … AN YR … MKAY.

lessons.title: Putting it together: FizzBuzz
lessons.summary: Loops, MOD, decisions and SMOOSH in one program.

sections.p: FizzBuzz counts from 1, but says FIZZ for multiples of 3, BUZZ for multiples of 5 and FIZZBUZZ for both. The loop counter starts at 0, so k holds the number to say, one more than the counter. MOD OF k AN 3 is 0 exactly when k divides by 3. Testing for 15 first stops the single words from winning.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A k
IM IN YR count UPPIN YR n TIL BOTH SAEM n AN 15
  k R SUM OF n AN 1
  BOTH SAEM MOD OF k AN 15 AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      VISIBLE "FIZZBUZZ"
    MEBBE BOTH SAEM MOD OF k AN 3 AN 0
      VISIBLE "FIZZ"
    MEBBE BOTH SAEM MOD OF k AN 5 AN 0
      VISIBLE "BUZZ"
    NO WAI
      VISIBLE k
  OIC
IM OUTTA YR count
KTHXBYE
sections.out:
1
2
FIZZ
4
BUZZ
FIZZ
7
8
FIZZ
BUZZ
11
FIZZ
13
14
FIZZBUZZ

sections.p: SMOOSH can grow a YARN one piece at a time. This builds a times-table row and prints it once at the end.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A row ITZ ""
IM IN YR t UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 5
  row R SMOOSH row AN PRODUKT OF 3 AN SUM OF i AN 1 AN " " MKAY
IM OUTTA YR t
VISIBLE "3 TIMEZ = " row
KTHXBYE

sections.p: You have met nearly all of LOLCODE 1.2. Try changing these programs in lci: FizzBuzz up to 100, a function that says whether a number is prime, or a countdown that reads its start with GIMMEH, which reads a line the user types into a variable as a YARN.

options: Otherwise 15 would match 3 first and print only FIZZ
MOD OF needs the biggest number first
practice.answer: Otherwise 15 would match 3 first and print only FIZZ
practice.why: Only the first matching part of an O RLY? runs.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
VISIBLE MOD OF 12 AN 3
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 12 divides by 3 exactly, so there is no remainder.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A s ITZ ""
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 3
  s R SMOOSH s AN i MKAY
IM OUTTA YR l
VISIBLE s
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Each round adds the counter to the end of s: 0, then 1, then 2.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR n TIL BOTH SAEM n AN 6
  BOTH SAEM MOD OF n AN 2 AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      VISIBLE n!
  OIC
IM OUTTA YR l
KTHXBYE
practice.why: n runs from 0 to 5, and only the even ones print.

options: Reads a typed line into x
practice.answer: Reads a typed line into x
practice.why: GIMMEH is LOLCODE's input; the value is always a YARN.

I HAS A s ITZ ""
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 4
  BOTH SAEM MOD OF SUM OF i AN 1 AN 2 AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY

    NO WAI

VISIBLE s

VISIBLE BOTH SAEM MOD OF 10 AN 5 AN 0
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 10 divides by 5 with remainder 0, so BOTH SAEM … AN 0 is WIN.

lessons.title: More SMOOSH and numbers as yarn
lessons.summary: Build longer strings and turn numbers into text.

sections.p: SMOOSH joins values into one YARN. Numbers are printed in decimal when smooshed, so you can build a label and a count in one go.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 3
I HAS A msg ITZ SMOOSH "NUTZ = " AN n MKAY
VISIBLE msg
KTHXBYE

sections.p: Grow a string across a loop by smooshing the old value with a new piece each time.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A s ITZ ""
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 3
  s R SMOOSH s AN "HA" MKAY
IM OUTTA YR l
VISIBLE s
KTHXBYE

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A x ITZ 2
VISIBLE SMOOSH "X" AN x MKAY
KTHXBYE
practice.why: SMOOSH joins with nothing in between.

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A s ITZ "A"
s R SMOOSH s AN "B" AN "C" MKAY
VISIBLE s
KTHXBYE
practice.why: Each AN piece is appended in order.

lessons.title: Project: fizz-buzz lines
lessons.summary: A tiny loop that builds labelled lines with SMOOSH.

sections.p: Count from 1 to 5. For each number, print a line that starts with the number and then either FIZZ (multiples of 3), BUZZ (multiples of 5), or NUTZ (everything else). Use MOD OF, O RLY? and SMOOSH together.
sections.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 0
I HAS A line ITZ ""
IM IN YR l UPPIN YR i TIL BOTH SAEM i AN 5
  n R SUM OF i AN 1
  line R SMOOSH n AN " " MKAY
  BOTH SAEM MOD OF n AN 3 AN 0
  O RLY?
    YA RLY
      line R SMOOSH line AN "FIZZ" MKAY
    MEBBE BOTH SAEM MOD OF n AN 5 AN 0
      line R SMOOSH line AN "BUZZ" MKAY
    NO WAI
      line R SMOOSH line AN "NUTZ" MKAY
  OIC
  VISIBLE line
IM OUTTA YR l
KTHXBYE

practice.code:
HAI 1.2
I HAS A n ITZ 6
BOTH SAEM MOD OF n AN 3 AN 0
O RLY?
  YA RLY
    VISIBLE "FIZZ"
  NO WAI
    VISIBLE "NUTZ"
OIC
KTHXBYE
practice.why: 6 mod 3 is 0.

practice.q: Which operator joins strings in LOLCODE?
practice.why: SMOOSH concatenates yarns.
